summary: Settings › Nushell has the controls two messages already pointed at. The line that named the `nu` in use is now `nu_controls` (src/finder/dialogs.rs): the status text (ID `nu-path`), a button `choose-nu` "Choose…" and a button `nu-auto` that reads "Find Automatically" while a path is chosen and "Look Again" when none is chosen and none was found; it isn't there when the `nu` in use was found by looking. `prompt_choose_nu` asks for one file with the system's chooser, keeps the path as returned, and shows a Warning when the chooser can't open. `Finder::set_nu_path` (src/finder/mod.rs) sets `nu_path`, publishes it as a shared setting, has `look_for_nu` find the `nu` again and refreshes every window. `look_for_nu` writes `AppState.nu` only when another `nu` was found. Every browser observes `AppState` (`cx.observe_global`, beside the file clipboard's observer in `Finder::new`) and runs `nu_changed`: it clears and reads again its Nushell actions, Nushell's colors and editor when that option is on, the previews (cached and still loading) and Quick Look's explore state, asks again for what is on screen, and resets the filter so it runs again. `Finder::new` looks for `nu` again when `reread_file` brought in another `nu_path` (a hand edit), and only then. The filter bar's and Rename's messages for a missing `nu` now end with "Set its path in Settings."
changelog: Settings › Nushell can choose which `nu` fffinder uses. **Choose…** picks it with the file chooser and saves it as `nu_path`; **Find Automatically** goes back to looking on `PATH` and in the usual install folders, and **Look Again** looks once more when none was found, for a `nu` installed while fffinder is running. The choice is used at once in every tab and window, with no restart: Nushell actions, filters, previews, Quick Look's explore mode, and Nushell's file colors are read again with it. The line beside the buttons names the `nu` in use, and says so when the chosen file isn't there and another one is used instead. Before, the messages for a missing `nu` said to set its path in Settings, which had no control for it: the path had to be typed into settings.json, followed by a restart. A `nu_path` edited into settings.json by hand now also applies when the next tab or window opens. This helps most when fffinder is opened from the Dock or a desktop menu and `nu` was installed with nix, mise, or asdf, which such an app can't find on its own.
behaviour_changes: Settings › Nushell: a new "Choose…" button on the first line opens the system's file chooser for one file (prompt "Choose"), saves it as `nu_path` and uses it at once.

Same line: "Find Automatically" while a path is chosen (clears `nu_path`, looks on PATH and in the usual folders); "Look Again" when nothing is chosen and no `nu` was found; no second button when the `nu` in use was found by looking.

The line's text: paths under the home folder start with `~` ("Using ~/.cargo/bin/nu" where it said "Using /Users/me/.cargo/bin/nu"); two new sentences for a chosen file that isn't there ("… wasn’t found, so … is used." and "… wasn’t found, and no other nu was found."); text too long for the line is cut with an ellipsis and shown whole in a tooltip.
The two buttons are extra small, the height of the line; everything below that line in Settings sits half a point lower (measured: the row is 20 points tall where the text was 19.5).

A change of the `nu` in use, from those buttons or from a hand-edited `nu_path` when a tab or window opens, takes effect in every tab, split pane and window without a restart. Nushell actions are read again, and emptied when no `nu` is left. Nushell's colors and editor are read again when that option is on; names are uncolored until the read returns. The preview on screen is loaded again (Preview Pane, column view's card, gallery, Quick Look), also one that was still loading. Quick Look's explore mode opens the file again, at its top level. An active filter runs again from scratch: the rows show unfiltered until it answers, and what is selected stays selected.
A hand-edited `nu_path` in settings.json is applied when the next tab or window opens. Before, it needed a restart.
If the file chooser can't open (in `--term`, or on Linux without a desktop portal), a warning notification says "Couldn’t open the file chooser: <reason>". Add Folder… still fails silently there.
The filter bar's error and the Rename-several-items warning for a missing `nu` now end with "Set its path in Settings."

Unchanged: which `nu` is found at startup, `find_nu` itself, and everything while the `nu` in use doesn't change (choosing the file already in use reads nothing again). The Nushell panel's last result stays as it is.
left_out: Running the chosen file to see that it is `nu` (the plan's optional `nu --version` check). Any file is accepted; the manual says so, and what uses Nushell then fails with an error that names the file.
The plan's optional unit test for `find_nu`: the function is unchanged.
A test of the warning for a chooser that can't open: the test platform can only answer a path prompt with a path or with none. The implementer tried the branch once with a throwaway edit; I read it.
The Nushell panel's last result isn't run again: a "not found" result stays until the pipeline is run.
A preview in the open Rename-several-items dialog isn't made again when the `nu` changes in another window; Return in its field makes it again.
`cargo clippy --features term` was not run: src/term is untouched and no signature it calls changed. macOS and Windows were not compiled here; the change has no cfg code.
CHANGELOG.md is not edited, as the guide says; the entry is in the commit message.
review_fixes: A preview that was still being read when the `nu` changed kept what the old `nu` made of it, or what none did. `nu_changed` cleared `previews` and asked again through `selection_changed`, but `ensure_preview` returns early while a load for the path is in `preview_tasks`, so the load started with the old `nu` finished and was cached, until Refresh. With a wrong pick that hangs, that window is the preview's 10 seconds. `nu_changed` now also clears `preview_tasks`, which drops those loads. New test a_preview_still_being_read_is_read_again_with_the_nu_found (tests/controls.rs): it failed on the implementer's commit and passes with the one line.
docs/manual.md: Look Again is "shown when none is chosen and none was found"; it said "when none was found", and with a chosen file that isn't there the button reads Find Automatically.
Commit message: the paragraph on what is dropped names the preview.
notes:
Checked. check.sh printed CHECK OK: 664 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures (645 before the rebase, on the lane's own base) on the trunk commit ca4fbee8b9f49edffc479ebd908699ee2a1cb308. The lane was rebased once, onto 153eb8f (search results and Recents that follow the index), which came in during the review; the two touch `Finder::new` and src/finder/mod.rs in different places and share no state: `nu_changed` leaves the search and its `results_behind` alone, and a quiet search's answer goes through `rebuild_rows`, where a filter runs again as always.

Tests fail without the change. With `git diff <base> HEAD -- src crates` reverse-applied, the six tests of the implementer fail: five at the missing `choose-nu` or `nu-auto`, and a_new_tab_picks_up_a_hand_edited_nu_path at left None, right Some(fake-nu); applied again, git status was clean. The proof that counts more: with only the observer's body taken out (`cx.observe_global::<AppState>` doing nothing), all six fail at assertions about the app (tests/controls.rs:2561 and 2639, tests/finder.rs:2062, tests/settings.rs:166 and 189, tests/settings_file.rs:118, as the files are on the trunk; I ran this before the rebase, which moved only the one in tests/finder.rs). The seventh test, mine, fails without the `preview_tasks.clear()` line. All seven pass with SEED=0, 1, 7, 42, 99, 1234 and 31337, and with `nu` hidden (`unshare -m` and /dev/null mounted over /usr/local/bin/nu), where two of them skip. settings_nu_choice is the one that sees the actions emptied when no `nu` is left, and only there: the implementer took the four clearing lines out and saw it fail without a `nu` and pass with one; I ran it as it is.

Looked at the window myself (pictures choose-nu-path-review-*.png, 1100x1150 so the whole dialog shows): `nu` found by looking; a chosen file in use; a chosen file that isn't there, with the tooltip, dark; the same with no other `nu`, dark; no `nu`; and a window 700 points wide at 150% text size, where the line's text is cut and both buttons keep their size while the rows around it run off the edge (see Found, not fixed).

Probes, not kept. (1) Two windows and a split pane: a `nu` chosen in one window's Settings is the other window's and the pane's at once (their `nu_path`, their actions read again, the other window's Settings line), and Find Automatically from the second window undoes it in the first. (2) `set_nu_path` twice in one update, both ways round: every tab ends with the last one's actions and colors, none with the first one's. (3) The column view's card, the gallery, and Quick Look from the list and the icon view each show a script colored by Nushell after Look Again finds a `nu`. (4) A search with a filter on: a wrong pick shows the filter's error with the file's name and the rows unfiltered, Find Automatically filters them again, and the selection stays through both. (5) Settings' heights, see the first doubt.

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt a user, and what the code says.
(1) A tab is disturbed when nothing changed for it, or left with what the old `nu` gave. Every browser reloads on any write to `AppState`. Its only writer after startup is `look_for_nu` (grep for global_mut and set_global in src, tests and examples; `init` sets it once, before any window), and it writes only when another `nu` was found. The reload keeps the selection (tried, with a filter running again under it), and by my reading of `rebuild_rows` and `sync_root_column`, which remap by path, the scroll position and the column view's panes; it doesn't touch a search. What it did leave behind was a preview still loading: fixed, see review_fixes. Actions, colors, the filter and explore mode were already dropped while loading (each replaces its task).
(2) A wrong pick that hides a working `nu` and can't be undone. Any existing file is accepted and overrides what looking would find. The line then says "Using <that file>", every use of Nushell fails with an error that names it, and Find Automatically is on the line whenever a path is chosen, whether its file is there or not (`chosen.is_some() || in_use.is_none()`). Clearing it is saved like any shared setting (`settings_changed`, then `Config::save_changes`, which writes the field as null). What nothing prevents: the chosen file is run with `nu`'s arguments by every tab for its actions, by previews, by filters, by the colors' login shell and by Open Nushell Here, until the choice is undone. The runs in the background are each stopped after 10 or 15 seconds; the one in a terminal isn't.
(3) Settings' layout. One line, as the brief asked: the text gives way, the buttons don't. See the first doubt for the height.

Doubts that remain.
1. Only Linux was built and run. The brief's main risk is Settings' height on macOS, where tests click lower controls without scrolling. Measured in the 1536x1080 test window with the Applications row that only macOS has forced on (`if cfg!(target_os = "macos")` set to true for the probe): at 110% text size the centre of `nu-text-bigger` is at y=985.25, where the implementer had it, with the Done button's top at 1012 and the dialog's scroll area ending at 996 by the implementer's measure, so 10.75 points to spare; it was 984.75 before this change. `sidebar-list` is below the fold there (1069), as before. At 100%: `choose-nu` and `nu-auto` 761.5, `use-nu-env` 847.5, `nu-text-bigger` 906. A Mac's own fonts may lay the rows out a little differently; this change moves them by half a point.
2. macOS's open panel is set not to resolve aliases (gpui-pre-macos-0.3.10/src/platform.rs, `setResolvesAliases(false)`), so a link should come back as chosen. Read, not run. It hides `~/.nix-profile` and the like; the manual says to paste the path.
3. Look Again gives no sign when it still finds nothing: the line beside it goes on saying that `nu` was not found.
4. The warning for a chooser that can't open doesn't say what to do instead. The manual does (settings.json), and Settings shows the file's path at its bottom.
5. A change of `nu` starts one `nu` per tab and pane for the actions, and a login shell each with Nushell's colors on, all at once. Opening the tabs one by one did the same over time.
6. Choosing the very path that is already in use reads nothing again, also when the file there was replaced in the meantime. Find Automatically and then Choose… does.
7. What needs a real `nu` to be tested is only tested where one is installed (here and in CI, through setup-nu): the preview and the filter with a real one in what_waited…, a_preview_still…, the explore reset, Look Again across tabs.
8. Extra-small buttons and `~` in the line are the implementer's calls, kept: buttons the size of Add Folder… make the row 5 points taller by the implementer's measure, which is half of what macOS has to spare above.

For briefs still to come.
- stale-previews-and-cancel: `nu_changed` (src/finder/mod.rs) clears `previews` and `preview_tasks`, sets `explore = None`, and calls `selection_changed`. Your stamp `(modified, size)` can't tell which `nu` made a preview, so a change of `nu` still has to drop every cached and every loading preview: with "`ensure_preview` returns when the in-flight stamp equals the entry's", a load started with the old `nu` would win again, and a_preview_still_being_read_is_read_again_with_the_nu_found (tests/controls.rs) fails. If you add `forget_previews`, use it in `nu_changed` and have it drop the loads too. Your part C is the stuck spinner the implementer here ran into (see Found, not fixed). `Explore` gets a `modified` in your plan; `nu_changed` drops the whole of it.
- filter-stale-keep-set: `nu_changed` resets the five fields `set_filter` resets (`filter_keep`, `filter_source`, `filter_error`, `filtering`, `filter_task`) and calls `rebuild_rows`. If you add filter state or tie the keep set to its source, reset it there as well, or give the two a helper. what_waited_for_a_nu_runs_with_the_one_chosen_in_settings pins that the filter runs again with the new `nu`. The missing-`nu` error now ends with "Set its path in Settings."
- search-settings-hints-steppers, search-settings-without-effect, search-roots-notes-dedupe: you change Settings above the Nushell section. The heights under the first doubt are what you start from: with macOS's row, at 110%, `nu-text-bigger` has 10.75 points left, so the Allow typos row (about 42) puts it below the fold, and settings_text_sizes needs to scroll before its click, as tests/folder_tree.rs does for `sidebar-list`. The new tests here click `choose-nu`, `nu-auto` and `use-nu-env` at 100% only, with 150 points and more to spare. The first line under NUSHELL is now `nu_controls(finder, &view, window, cx)`; `fit::with_cut_off_text` on a `flex_1().min_w_0().truncate()` div is how its text gives way to the buttons, which a root's note beside a path could use too. search-roots-notes-dedupe: `prompt_choose_nu` stands right after `prompt_add_root` and shows a Warning when the chooser can't open; Add Folder… still drops that error, and you are editing it.
- restore-session-tabs: every browser observes `AppState` and compares `nu_path` before and after `reread_file` in `Finder::new`. Building several in one update is fine: the lookup runs for the first one that sees another `nu_path` in the file, and a browser made in the same update isn't called for a write that came before it (the observer is switched on by a deferred effect). tests/settings_file.rs has a new test after a_new_tab_picks_up_a_hand_edit.
- focus-lost-recovery (in a lane now): the `subscriptions` vec in `Finder::new` has one more entry at its end, `cx.observe_global::<AppState>(|this, cx| this.nu_changed(cx))`, with a two-line comment; expect a textual conflict if yours goes at the end too.
- empty-state-messages (in a lane now): `filter_error` is cleared and set again by `nu_changed`; its text for a missing `nu` changed as above.
- quick-look-empty-state: `nu_changed` drops `explore` and has `selection_changed` open the file again; tests/finder.rs has a new test after quick_look_explores_structured_files, which drives Quick Look's window while Settings is open in the browser's.
- preview-page-keys: your plan calls `selection_changed`; `nu_changed` calls it too, with the selection as it was, so it has to stay harmless when nothing was selected anew.
- files-changed-off-thread: `check_for_changes` is as it was; `user_actions_stamp` is set to None by `nu_changed` and comes back with the next read.
- tab-drop-and-close: the new observer holds no window, unlike the subscriptions made with `subscribe_in_window`, so a browser needs nothing done about it.
- Whoever rebases next: this commit added `look_for_nu` after `impl Global for AppState`, six lines at the top of `Finder::new`, `set_nu_path` and `nu_changed` after `terminal_setting` in src/finder/mod.rs; `prompt_choose_nu` after `prompt_add_root` and `nu_status` and `nu_controls` before `custom_terminal_hint` in src/finder/dialogs.rs; three tests after settings_terminal_choice in tests/controls.rs, two after a_column_another_tab_adds_is_filled_in_for_this_tabs_results in tests/settings.rs, one each in tests/finder.rs and tests/settings_file.rs as said above; three bullets under Settings › Nushell, the `nu_path` row and the --term note in docs/manual.md.

Found, not fixed (on the trunk before this change, outside this brief).
- From the implementer: after an appearance change (Cmd+Shift+D, or Settings), `previews.clear()` isn't followed by a new request, so the Preview Pane stays on its loading state until the selection changes; the gallery asks again when it draws. That is part C of stale-previews-and-cancel.
- Add Folder… in Settings does nothing, and says nothing, when the file chooser can't open (`prompt_add_root` drops the error): in `--term` and on Linux without a desktop portal.
- Settings is 600 points wide and two of its rows don't fit that with the fonts here: the third switch of Appearance reads "Remember each folder's vi" and ends at the dialog's edge, and with a long terminal name ("Automatic (System Default (x-terminal-emulator))") Try It hangs over the right margin. Both are in every picture of this change, the before one too. In a narrow window at 150% the letter case buttons and the terminal menu run off the edge as well.
- A wrong `nu`, chosen now or typed into settings.json before, is run by Open Nushell Here in a terminal without a word. That was so for a hand-edited `nu_path` already.
